target_customer: Medspas, plastic surgery and wellness clinics that take cash payments
problem: Aesthetic clinics juggle separate front desk, charting, payments and marketing tools built for salons rather than automation.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription EMR and practice management with an AI employee
product_category: AI EMR and practice management for medical aesthetics

competitors.name: Moxie
competitors.what: Medspa management platform with EMR, checkout and payments

competitors.name: Podium
competitors.what: AI operating system for aesthetic practices with an AI employee for leads and booking

technical_complexity.rationale: A full EMR, POS and marketing suite with HIPAA compliance, e-prescribing and AI agents is a wide build for two founders, though each part is standard.

defensibility.rationale: EMR data and workflows lock in clinics, but established vendors and funded rivals offer similar AI features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals shipped AI scribe and AI employee features in early 2026; no source shows Tepali being copied or bought yet.

market_need_then: Cash-pay aesthetics and wellness clinics are growing and typically use fragmented tools; many vendors market AI features, which signals demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short direct fragments such as A text, not a ticket

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is new; only the YC launch and a magazine feature exist.

outcome_analysis: Tepali is a Winter 2026 company with two founders whose backgrounds fit a vertical software play, one from Dripos and one from Rilla. No funding, exit or traction is verified. The medspa software space already has funded players and AI entrants, so the early outcome depends on distribution and speed.
notes: One aggregator lists 500K pre-seed in March 2026, but the same figure appears for a different company (Decoda Health), so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Founders' roles both listed as CEO on YC. Outcome search found only unrelated Moxie news. No brand origin found.
